sentences.text:
Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
 Office Notes,
Sl. Date reports,
No. orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order

Registrar's  order with  Signatures  IA No. 1 of 2022  In  CRJA No. 52 of 2022  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.

The present appellant- Dheeraj Singh Kushwaha has been convicted pursuant to the judgment and order dated 10.05.2022, passed by the 2nd Addl. Session Judge, Haldwani Nainital in S.T. No.
27 of 2020, State vs. Dheeraj Singh Kushwaha whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 323, 376 read with Section 511, 354(ka)(1), 354 (gha), 506 IPC read with Section 66E and 67 of the I.T. Act and the maximum sentence as awarded by the Trial court is 7 years rigorous imprisonment with the fine of Rs. 50,000/-
2.
This is an admitted appeal, admitted on 26.07.2022.
The Trial Court record has also been received and the paper book is prepared.

3. Since, Ms. Akleema Parveen, the Amicus Curiae for the appellant is not present and this is a jail appeal and the appellant is seeking bail on the ground that he has already completed more than half of the sentence, therefore, Ms. Arushi Batra, learned Advocate is now appointed as an Amicus Curiae for the appellant.
4. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned Brief Holder for the State.
It is submitted by the learned Amicus Curiae for the appellant that the appellant was arrested on 19.01.2020 and since then he is in jail.
It is submitted that the appellant is in long incarceration and he has no previous criminal history which itself is reflected from para 189 of the judgment.

7. Learned State Counsel has not disputed this fact that the appellant was arrested on 19.01.2020 and he was never been granted bail, and, therefore, he served more than half of the sentence CRJA/52/2022 on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188515947/
1 awarded by the Trial Court.

8. After taking into consideration that the appellant has already completed more than half of the sentence and has no previous criminal history and this appeal is of the year 2022 and there is no possibility that the appeal be expedited shortly, thus, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, this Court is of the view that the appellant deserves for bail.
9. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

10. Let the appellant be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
Realisation of fine shall also remain suspended during the pendency of the appeal.
11. List this case for final hearing in the month of August 2025.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 08.11.2024 Parul CRJA/52/2022 on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188515947/
2
